title: Fast-dissociating but highly specific antibodies are novel tools in biology, especially useful for multiplex super-resolution microscopy
protocol: Prepare three non-treated 96-well tissue culture plates for each 96-well plate used to culture hybridoma clones.
Put 200 μl of fresh culture medium in each well of the new plates.
Detach hybridoma clones from tissue culture plates using a multichannel pipette.
Use a new pipette tip for each well to prevent cross-contamination.
Suspend the detached hybridomas by aspirating and dispensing 250 μL of culture medium three times per well.
Aspirate a total of 300 μL of cell suspension from each original well.
Dispense 100 μl into each of three wells on three 96-well plates.
Culture the hybridomas at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2 for 2 days.
Prepare amine-functionalized 96-well glass-bottom plates.
Purchase custom requested 96-well plates with a glass bottom equivalent to a high-precision No. 1.5 coverslip and low-bottom plastic frame from Matsunami Glass IND LTD or similar manufacturers.
Weigh 4.93 mg of sulfo-SANPAH in a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 100 μL of DMSO to the sulfo-SANPAH and completely dissolve using a vortex mixer for 15-30 seconds.
Add 10 mL of PBS, pH 7.0, to the dissolved sulfo-SANPAH solution.
Vortex the sulfo-SANPAH-PBS solution once again for 15-30 seconds.
Keep sulfo-SANPAH at -20°C and avoid humid air to prevent moisture sensitivity.
Prepare additional 96-well plates for positive control antibodies.
Include antibody-free culture medium as a negative control.
Use commercial antibodies as positive controls if the EGFP-antigen has an epitope tag for purification, such as FLAG-tag.
Apply 100 μL of sulfo-SANPAH solution to each well.
Wrap the plates with an aluminum foil to shield from light.
Incubate the plates at 20°C–25°C for 2 hours gently mixing the solution on a shaker at ∼10 rpm.
Remove the sulfo-SANPAH solution from each well with a multichannel aspirator.
Rinse wells three times with PBS pH 7.0.
Incubate for 3 min at 20°C–25°C for each rinse.
Add 300 μL of 10 mg/mL Protein A/G stock solution to 10 mL PBS, pH 7.0.
Mix by gently inverting the tube.
Apply 100 μL to each well.
Place the plates on a UV transilluminator and select “High” for MUV21-365 (NIPPON Genetics).
Incubate for 30 min under UV light.
Gently rock the plates on a shaker for 30 min at 20°C–25°C.
Remove the Protein A/G solution from each well.
Add 300 μL of 3% BSA dissolved in PBS to block non-specific protein binding sites.
Incubate the plate for 16–18 h at 4°C with gentle shaking.
Prepare three new 96-well non-treated tissue culture plates for each 96-well plate of hybridomas to be subcultured.
Aliquot 200 μL of culture medium to each well of the new plates.
Suspend hybridoma clones in the original 96-well plates using a 96-well multichannel pipetting instrument.
Dispense 100 μL of suspended hybridomas into each well of three fresh plates containing 200 μL of culture medium.
Culture hybridomas at 37°C in 5% CO2 while antibodies are being screened over a period of 4 and 5 days.
Sample culture supernatants by suspending cells in the plates not used for subculture using a 96-well multichannel pipettor.
Aspirate cell suspensions and transfer them into 96-1-mL deep-well plates.
Centrifuge the plates at ∼180 × g for 2 min to pellet the cells.
Apirate the culture supernatants and store in new 96-1-mL deep-well plates.
Apply a sealable lid to prevent evaporation of supernatants.
Store the plates at 4°C.
Add 1/100 volume of 3% sodium azide (NaN3) to each well for long-term storage of culture supernatants.
Rinse each well of the 96-well glass-bottom plates using PBS.
Incubate for 3 min at 20°C–25°C for each rinse.
Apply 300 μL of culture supernatant for each well of the glass-bottom plates.
Incubate for 16–18 h at 4°C.
Power up the TIRF microscope.
Adjust the angle of laser light to achieve TIRF illumination.
Place a new 96-well glass-bottom plate on the microscope.
Add a solution of calibration beads to a few wells in the plate.
Tilt the laser angle stepwise from the epi-fluorescence position.
Find the narrow range of angles where the background fluorescence intensity suddenly decreases.
Avoid an angle of TIRF illumination that results in interference fringes.
Remove the unbound components of culture supernatants by rinsing the wells of the 96-well glass-bottom three times for 3 min using 300 μL of HEPES-KCl-Tx buffer.
Prepare EGFP-antigen solutions as described in the materials and equipment section.
Test the EGFP-antigen using an antibody-free glass surface treated with culture medium.
Test the glass-surface with an immobilized positive control antibody, such as against the antigen of interest.
Use antibodies against epitope tags like FLAG-tag as positive controls if applicable.
Apply EGFP-antigen at various concentrations to determine the maximum concentration without non-specific binding.
Set up imaging conditions, including laser power and exposure time, using the positive control antibody.
Place the glass-bottom plate upside-down on a paper towel before use.
Thinly spread immersion oil on the lens-side of the entire glass-bottom plate.
Place the glass-bottom plate in an upright position without disturbing the immersion oil.
Add 100 μL of EGFP-antigen solution to each well.
Acquire short time-lapse movies sequentially for each well, consisting of 50 frames.
Set the exposure time to 50 ms and the laser power (473 nm) to 4–6 mW.
Use an Evolve 512 EMCCD camera with EM Gain set at 300, Gain State 3, and 10 MHz.
Control the automated stage and autofocusing device using a MetaMorph macroinstruction.
Scan plates treated with positive and negative controls before scanning antibodies of interest.
Start scanning within 5 minutes after adding EGFP-antigen solution to each well.
Complete screening within 1 hour from the start of adding EGFP-antigen solution.
Compare the density of bound EGFP-antigen in each well with a negative control well treated with antibody-free culture medium.
Identify antibodies immobilized in the well as showing a positive response if the density of bound EGFP-antigen is larger than that in a negative control well.
Subculture “positive” clones by suspending cells in three wells across three tissue culture plates (total ∼900 μL).
Transfer suspended cells to a well of a non-treated, 24-well plate.
Add 2 mL of fresh culture medium to the well containing transferred cells.
Dispense 1 mL of the total ∼3 mL into two unused wells for subculturing hybridomas.
Culture each identified hybridoma clone using two or three wells of a 24-well tissue culture plate.
Subculture cells from one well into three additional wells by adding 2 mL of culture medium and suspending gently.
Cryopreserve cells from the remaining one or two wells not used for subculture.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at approximately 180 × g for 2 minutes.
Remove the supernatant culture medium.
Add 1 mL of CELLBANKER1 to the cells from one well and suspend gently (use 2 mL for cells collected from two wells).
Transfer the cell suspension to cryotubes.
Freeze the cryotubes at -80°C in a microtube storage box.
Collect culture supernatants after cells are centrifuged for cryopreservation and use them to evaluate antibody secretion.
Store culture supernatants up to ∼1 month at 4°C after adding 1/100 volume of 3% sodium azide (NaN3).
Aliquot and freeze hybridoma supernatants at -20°C or preferably at -80°C for longer-term storage.
Check a small quantity of each monoclonal antibody for retention of function following a freeze thaw cycle.
Prepare 4–6 tubes of cryopreserved cells for each hybridoma clone.
Subculture hybridoma clones until obtaining ∼12 mL of culture supernatant to obtain monoclonal antibodies.
Isolate monoclonal populations using a limiting dilution technique.
Suspend cells gently using a pipette.
Determine the density of cells using an EVE automatic cell counter or an inexpensive hemocytometer after trypan blue staining.
Dilute a cell suspension to achieve approximately 1 cell per 100 μL of culture medium.
For example, add 10 μL of a cell suspension containing 1 × 10^4 cells/mL to 1 mL of culture medium to achieve 100 cells/mL.
Add 10 μL of diluted cell suspension to 10 mL of culture medium to achieve one cell per 100 μL (0.1 cell/mL).
Aliquot 100 μL of this suspension to each well of a 96-well tissue culture plate.
Add 100 μL of fresh culture medium two days later and again at four days after starting the limiting dilution.
Incubate the plate until cells proliferate.
Identify wells in which cells proliferate.
Subculture the monoclonal populations.
Cryopreserve the cells.
Obtain hybridoma culture supernatants for evaluation.
Prepare a new Protein A/G-coated glass-bottom plate.
Apply hybridoma culture supernatants containing antibodies and incubate for 16-18 hours at 4°C to immobilize the antibodies.
Remove the unbound components of culture supernatants by rinsing the wells using 300 μL of HEPES-KCl-Tx buffer.
Incubate for 3 min at 20°C–25°C for each rinse.
Place the 96-well glass-bottom plate on the stage of the TIRF microscope.
Remove the HEPES-KCl-Tx buffer and apply diluted EGFP-antigen just prior to starting acquisition of time-lapse images.
Dilute the EGFP-antigen to 0.1 nM–1 nM to decrease the density of bound EGFP-antigen molecules.
Acquire time-lapse images at appropriate intervals.
Try several time-intervals ranging from 50 ms to 10 s.
Find an interval achieving a 30%–50% exchange of bound EGFP-antigen molecules per frame.
For fast-dissociating antibodies, acquire images using the stream acquisition mode of MetaMorph at 50–300 ms intervals.
For slow-dissociating antibodies, acquire images every 500 ms to 10 s with a 50-ms exposure time using a time-lapse acquisition mode of MetaMorph.
Set the laser power (473 nm) to 4–6 mW and adjust depending on the exposure time.
Use the Evolve 512 EMCCD camera with EM Gain (EM = 300, Gain State 3, 10 MHz).
Track the regression of bound EGFP-antigen molecules.
Fit a one-phase decay model to determine the appropriate interval of acquisition.
Fit a one-phase decay model to the regression curve of bound EGFP-antigen molecules.
Determine the koff between antibodies and epitopes using GraphPad Prism software for kinetic analyses.
Prepare weakly-fixed Xenopus XTC cells expressing EGFP-actin.
Immerse the cells in HEPES-KCl-Tx buffer supplemented with glucose, glucose oxidase, and catalase.
Set the laser power and exposure time to cause photobleaching at a rate approximately 10-fold slower than the koff.
For 2 mL of hybridoma culture supernatant, add 20 μL of Protein A beads suspended in PBS and incubate for 16–18 h at 4°C with gentle rotation at 10-15 rpm.
Wash beads three times in 500 μL of PBS-EDTA pH 7.0.
Centrifuge washed beads at 500 × g for 1 min.
Resuspend pellet in 70–80 μL of PBS-EDTA pH 7.0.
Dissolve 50 μg of DyLight488-maleimide or DyLight550-maleimide in 5 μL of DMSO to obtain a 10 μg/μL dye solution.
Mix well using a vortex machine for 30–60 seconds.
Dissolve DyLight488-maleimide or DyLight550-maleimide dry powder in 300 μL methanol.
Dispense the solution into Eppendorf tubes by 15 μL portions.
Evaporate the methanol under reduced pressure.
Store the dye aliquots tightly capped and in the dark at -20°C with desiccant.
Add 5 μL of dye dissolved in DMSO to the bead suspension.
Incubate the beads shielded from light for 2 hours at 20°C–25°C.
Gently mix the beads using a rotator at 10–15 rpm during incubation.
Label antibodies via lysine residues using DyLight488-NHS-ester or DyLight550-NHS-ester.
Remove unreacted dye with five washes of the beads in 500 μL of PBS.
Add 20 μl of 0.01 mg/ml Papain solution and incubate at 37°C for 1 hour, shaking every 15 minutes to suspend the beads.
Centrifuge the beads to recover supernatant containing Fab probes.
Add 2 μl of 0.1 mg/ml Leupeptin dissolved in PBS to inhibit proteolytic activity of papain.
Aliquot the Fab probe solution and store at -80°C.
Supplement an additional 1 μg/mL of Leupeptin to the working solutions of Fab probes.
